text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Drugs go up in smoke. Police start destroy 7.5 tons of drugs seized in a container at Malta Freeport last week on their way to Romania from Singapore.
- Police suspect false Lm10 ($3 approx) notes were printed in Sicily and introduced in Malta circulation through a casino.

- More questions on Begrade crash. Jugoslav Vreme magazine says crashed Ilyushin 76 had been chartered by Jugoimport, the bigest arms exporting firm in Yugoslavia. The aircraft was bound for Malta with a cargo due to have been unloaded for shipment to Libya through Malta Freeport. The Malta government said aircraft documents showed it was carrying wheels for agricultural equipment and sportswear. The shippers enclosed a declaration that they were not violating U.N. sanctions against Libya.
